skills.observableOutcome: Identifies the value of a digit in a three-digit number.
Solves an addition problem with two two-digit addends.
Compares lengths measured in centimeters.
Identifies a suitable habitat for an animal and connects living things to their environments.
Selects a familiar English word that completes a simple context sentence.
Recognizes a correctly ordered simple English sentence.
Identifies plants as living things using observable evidence such as growth and change.
Names common plant parts and connects selected parts with their functions and edible uses.
Traces familiar foods and useful materials to plant sources.
Describes early seed germination and identifies conditions that support seedling growth.
Compares plants fairly using observable features and consistent measurements.
Records visible changes during a simple supervised observation.
Observes plants safely and avoids tasting or damaging unknown plants.
Applies early grammar, word recognition, capitalization and punctuation conventions.
Identifies meaning and key details in short age-appropriate English texts.
Identifies the value of digits in two- and three-digit numbers.
Solves age-appropriate addition and subtraction problems.
Represents multiplication through equal groups and repeated addition.
Uses measurement ideas to solve simple practical problems.
Recognizes equal parts and applies simple measurement relationships.
Recognizes basic concepts about living things, materials and the Earth.
Identifies animals as living things using observable evidence.
Matches familiar young animals with adults and recognises that young animals can change as they grow.
Identifies suitable habitats by matching animal needs with available food, water and shelter.
Classifies familiar animals as vertebrates or invertebrates using the presence of a backbone.
Identifies adult insects using six legs and three main body regions, while distinguishing spiders.
Sequences and compares familiar animal life-cycle stages.
Explains how predator-prey relationships and observable adaptations can help animals survive.
Observes and identifies relevant visible features of familiar living things.
Classifies familiar animals using a stated scientific rule and explains the grouping.
Sequences stages in a life cycle using evidence from the activity.
Explains how an observable body feature can help an animal in a stated habitat.

optionRationales.a: A predator hunts another animal for food
optionRationales.b: A plant is not a predator
optionRationales.c: A predator feeds; it does not never eat

activities.prompt: In a simple example, a fox hunts a rabbit. Which animal is the prey?

optionRationales.a: The fox is the predator in this example
optionRationales.b: The rabbit is being hunted, so it is prey
optionRationales.c: Neither animal is a plant

activities.prompt: How can camouflage help a stick insect?

options.text: It makes the insect able to breathe underwater
It gives the insect more legs
It can help the insect blend in among branches

optionRationales.a: Camouflage is not an underwater breathing feature
optionRationales.b: Camouflage does not add legs
optionRationales.c: Matching the surroundings can make it harder to see

activities.prompt: A white animal is difficult to see on snow but easy to see on dark soil. What does this show?

options.text: Camouflage is useful when it matches the surroundings
Colour never affects how visible an animal is

optionRationales.a: Camouflage depends on the surroundings
optionRationales.b: Matching surroundings can reduce visibility
optionRationales.c: Colour can affect how visible an animal is

activities.prompt: How do a duck's webbed feet help it?

options.text: They help it push against water when swimming
They help it fly without wings

optionRationales.a: Webbed feet help a duck push against water
optionRationales.b: Webbed feet do not replace wings
optionRationales.c: Webbed feet are not food stores

activities.prompt: What is stored in a camel's hump?

options.text: Fat that can be used for energy

optionRationales.a: A camel's hump does not store a tank of water
optionRationales.b: The hump is not an air store
optionRationales.c: The hump stores fat that can be used for energy
